questions.title: Who will win the men's 200m at the 2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship?
questions.background: The inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship is scheduled for September 11–13, 2026, in Budapest.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official World Athletics results, supported by contemporaneous reporting of the championship. Resolution : Resolve to the athlete who wins the men's 200m final at the 2026 Ultimate Championship, scheduled for September 11–13, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The winning athlete's full name.

questions.title: Who will win Okinawa's 2026 gubernatorial election?
questions.background: Okinawa is Japan's southernmost prefecture, where the presence of US military bases is a major political issue.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official results announced by Okinawa's election authorities, either directly or as reported by reliable news organizations. Resolution : The question resolves when the winner of Okinawa's 2026 gubernatorial election is officially announced. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major final-weekend polling sweep published Sept 6 (one week before Sept 13 voting) shifts the race decisively toward five-party-backed challenger Genta Koja (0.53 -> 0.63) over two-term All-Okinawa incumbent Denny Tamaki (0.46 -> 0.365; 0.005 across four minor candidates): (1) Yomiuri Shimbun (Sep 3-6, phone+net, n=1,410) reports Koja clearly leading ('先行') with Tamaki trailing—noting 20% of 2022 Tamaki voters switched to Koja, 80% of 2022 Shimoji voters back Koja, and economy/prices (75%) dwarfs bases (45%); (2) Asahi Shimbun / Okinawa Times / QAB (Sep 5-6, phone+net) similarly reports Koja slightly ahead ('やや先行') with Tamaki chasing vigorously (40% undecided)—a striking signal given Okinawa Times/Asahi's historically All-Okinawa-favorable coverage; (3) Kyodo / Ryukyu Shimpo / OTV (Sep 5-6, pure RDD phone, 603 landline + 404 mobile) shows a dead heat ('横一線', <10% undecided), yet its internals also favor Koja: economy/tourism/jobs is the #1 issue (46%, breaking 70% Koja) vs bases (26%, breaking 80% Tamaki), and Henoko relocation support edges opposition 48%-46%. We cap Koja at 0.63 (leaving Tamaki 0.365) because pure phone polls remain tied, Tamaki leads ~60% of independents and 70+ voters (who turn out at higher rates), and 20-40% remain undecided in Yomiuri/Asahi.

questions.title: Which country will Washington propose as a possible venue for renewed trilateral Russia–Ukraine ceasefire talks by September 25, 2026?
questions.background: The United States has been involved in efforts to broker an end to the Russia–Ukraine war.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country publicly identified by Ukraine's president as Washington's proposed location for renewed talks involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine, using the proposal current as of September 25, 2026. A suggested location is sufficient; the talks need not have taken place. Resolution Date : 2026-09-25 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-09-08 recalibration from Reuters, Interfax-Ukraine, Kyiv Post, Euronews, Anadolu Agency, NV.ua, and Axios: (1) Correcting yesterday's UNGA overreaction, the actual Axios report and Zelenskyy's Sept 8 remarks clarify that New York/UNGA around Sept 20 is for a bilateral Trump-Zelenskyy meeting on winter Patriot air defense—not Washington's proposed trilateral venue—dropping United States sharply from 0.30 to 0.14 (retaining ~14% because Trump/Witkoff could still pitch a US venue after Trump's Sept 8 call with Putin emphasizing restored US-Russia ties). (2) In his Sept 8 WhatsApp press briefing, Zelenskyy explicitly named the three primary candidate venues for the renewed US-Ukraine-Russia trilateral talks: 'The meeting could be in the Emirates, Switzerland, Turkey, or in other countries. We have experience, and there are invitations from various nations.' (3) Switzerland rises 0.24 -> 0.27 as narrow #1: hosted the previous Feb 2026 Geneva trilateral round, is insulated from the Middle East war, and aligns with Zelenskyy's Sept 8 insistence (Euronews) that European allies must be at the table. (4) Turkey rises 0.21 -> 0.26 as near-co-favorite #2: explicitly named by Zelenskyy and directly fits the exact Sept 8 agenda he outlined (maritime grain export corridors, energy infrastructure, and POW exchanges). (5) United Arab Emirates jumps sharply 0.09 -> 0.21 (#3): despite Gulf war risks, Zelenskyy named 'the Emirates' first verbatim, reflecting Abu Dhabi's prior 2026 trilateral hosting, POW-exchange mediation role, and Witkoff/Kushner ties. (6) Saudi Arabia trims 0.05 -> 0.03 after being omitted from Zelenskyy's Sept 8 trio and struck by Houthi attacks across four cities today, leaving 0.09 residual (Qatar, Austria, Vatican, etc.).
